answer.cause: GitHub no longer accepts plain passwords for HTTPS authentication. You need a [personal access token (PAT)](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens) instead.
answer.explanation: GitHub blocked password-based authentication for security reasons. Now you must use a **personal access token (PAT)** as your password when pushing via HTTPS. This token acts like a password but is safer because it can be revoked if compromised.

When Git prompts for your password, paste the **PAT** instead of your GitHub password.
Retry pushing with your PAT. This should now work.

warnings: Never share your PAT with anyone or commit it to a repository. If you accidentally commit it, rotate the token immediately via GitHub settings and notify collaborators.

If you previously used your GitHub password and it was pushed to a remote, ensure no sensitive data (e.g., API keys, passwords) was committed. If so, rotate those secrets and clean up the repo using `git filter-repo` or contact collaborators to remove the commits.
If you still face issues, verify your SSH setup with `ssh -T git@github.com` (see [excerpt 2]). If you prefer SSH, switch your remote URL to use `git@github.com:user/repo.git` instead of HTTPS.
